beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: (1) infrastructure creation, which includes railway platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying, bridges (beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed, truss), and road construction (bituminous and concrete); and (2) a Ready Mix Concrete (RMC) plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Contracts are won through a tender process: clients float tenders, pre-bid meetings are held, the lowest quote wins a Letter of Acceptance, and the contractor deposits a performance guarantee before site handover.

The company's major clients include government bodies and state-owned enterprises: Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), and Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA). Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the orders on hand as of the filing date.
Revenue concentration is high: top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in FY2018.

The company's competitive strengths as stated in the DRHP include long-standing relationships with marquee clients (Western Railway since 2006), use of modern techniques like box-pushing, experienced management (over 20 years in the industry), a state-of-the-art facility, and a healthy order book.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over four years. The revenue figures for each year (in ₹ crore): FY2014: 86.61, FY2015: 90.21, FY2016: 74.53, FY2017: 73.44, FY2018: 60.53.

Profit after tax (PAT) was highly volatile: ₹0.96 crore in FY2014, ₹0.78 crore in FY2015, ₹0.33 crore in FY2016, ₹0.16 crore in FY2017, and a sharp jump to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018. The FY2018 spike is notable but unexplained in the filing.
Profit before interest, depreciation and tax (EBITDA) followed a similar pattern: ₹7.84 crore (FY2014), ₹9.46 crore (FY2015), ₹7.83 crore (FY2016), ₹6.76 crore (FY2017), ₹9.29 crore (FY2018).

Debt levels have been fluctuating. Long-term borrowings stood at ₹1.33 crore in FY2018, down from ₹6.73 crore in FY2015. Short-term borrowings, however, increased to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018 from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014.
The company reported negative cash flows in recent financial years, though exact figures are not disclosed in the extracted facts. The DRHP flags sustained negative cash flow as a risk.
A table of key financial metrics (revenue, PAT, EBITDA, borrowings) for all five reported years will be included.

beats.beat: The promoter and managing director is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issued capital. Post-issue, his stake will reduce but he will remain the controlling shareholder.

Two companies promoted by Mr. Mishra — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation of business.

Related party transactions include loans from key management personnel/board of directors amounting to ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties of ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.

None of the directors are on the RBI list of willful defaulters, and no criminal cases have been filed or investigations undertaken against any director. However, there is pending litigation disclosed, though details are not in the extracted excerpts.

The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the proposed project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed for fund deployment — deployment is at the discretion of management and the board, subject to audit committee oversight.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector in India is highly fragmented, working capital intensive, and contributes approximately 8% to India's GDP (at constant prices).

Key demand drivers include government flagship programs (100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, Power for All), eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including real estate and construction, and rising industrialization, urbanization, disposable income, and population growth.

India requires investment of ₹50 trillion (US$777.73 billion) in infrastructure by 2022 to achieve sustainable development. The logistics sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5%, from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020.
The filing acknowledges headwinds: slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized sectors; the market is highly fragmented.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based construction and infrastructure company with two operating segments: creation of infrastructure (railways, bridges, roads) and operation of a Ready Mix Concrete (RMC) plant.

The company is raising capital through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares on the SME Board of BSE, with the proceeds primarily earmarked for working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and general corporate purposes.

This IPO is an offer for sale? No, it is a fresh issue — the company will receive the funds, not existing shareholders. The promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, holds 90.949% pre-issue and will remain the controlling shareholder post-issue.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who A B Infrabuild is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each, at a price to be determined. It is a fresh issue with no offer for sale component.

Net proceeds are allocated to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed). The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, nor a monitoring agency to track fund deployment.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

beats.beat: Revenue concentration on Indian Railways: In FY2018, 57% of the company's revenue came from Indian Railways (primarily Western Railway). Loss of this client would cause a significant revenue dip.
Negative cash flows: The company has experienced sustained negative cash flow in recent financial years, which could impair its ability to fund operations and service debt.
Unsecured loans repayable on demand: As of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans that are repayable on demand. A demand for repayment could severely strain cash flow.
Promoter's struck-off companies: Two companies promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, raising governance concerns.
No independent project appraisal: The company has not engaged an independent agency to appraise the use of IPO proceeds, meaning investors rely solely on management's judgment for fund allocation.
